question: P and Q are two towns. A man drives from P to Q at an average speed of 50 km/h. He stops at Q for 4 hours and then heads back to P at an average speed of 40 km/h following the same route. What is his average speed (in km/h correct to two decimal places) if he takes 22 hours for the entire trip?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average driving speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂) = (2 × 50 × 40) ÷ (50 + 40) = 400/9 km/h.

Total driving time = Total time − Stoppage time = 22 − 4 = 18 hours.

Total distance = Average driving speed × Total driving time = (400/9) × 18 = 800 km.

Average speed for the entire trip = Total distance ÷ Total time = 800 ÷ 22 = 36.36 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.36 km/h.**
